zujose: Sign, Verify, Encrypt and Decrypt JSON Web Tokens

Source: R/zujose-package.R
zujose-package.Rd

Signs, verifies, encrypts and decrypts JSON Object Signing and Encryption ('JOSE') objects: JSON Web Signatures (RFC 7515) doi:10.17487/RFC7515 , JSON Web Encryption (RFC 7516) doi:10.17487/RFC7516 , JSON Web Keys (RFC 7517) doi:10.17487/RFC7517 and JSON Web Tokens (RFC 7519) doi:10.17487/RFC7519 , in the compact and JSON serializations. The caller names the algorithms it accepts, and tokens are checked against the current best practices of RFC 8725 doi:10.17487/RFC8725 . Written in R over 'zucrypt', so no system cryptography library is needed.

Details

Start with the Get started article, at https://pedrobtz.github.io/zujose/articles/zujose.html. The main functions are:

  • JWT: jwt_encode(), jwt_decode(), jwt_decoder().

  • JWS: jws_sign(), jws_verify().

  • JWE: jwe_encrypt(), jwe_decrypt().

  • Keys: jwk_oct(), jwk_generate(), as_jwk(), jwk_set(), as_jwk_set(), jwk_json(), jwk_pem().

  • Inspection: jose_peek(), zujose_info().

zujose never fetches anything: keys come only from the caller, as a key, a key set, or a function that returns one (a resolver).

Secrets in memory

zujose is pure R, and so are its keys: an oct secret, and the private members of an RSA, EC or X25519 key, are ordinary R vectors. R copies vectors freely and has no way to wipe one, so a secret may stay in memory after the key is gone, and may reach a saved workspace or a core dump. zujose never prints secret members and never puts them in an error message, but it cannot do more than that. Keep long-lived secrets out of saved workspaces (.RData) and load them from a secret store when they are needed.

Examples

key <- jwk_generate("oct", alg = "HS256")
jwt <- jwt_encode(list(sub = "user-1"), key, expires_in = 3600)
jwt_decode(jwt, key, algorithms = "HS256")$sub
#> [1] "user-1"
